To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the consensus sequences of the ends, and particularly the 5' ends, of L1 elements can vary depending on the methylation state of the host DNA and that the 5' region contains a putative open reading frame.

(1) the 5' region (the 5' UTR) of the 1,8 kb L1 is a CpG-rich region, which in human somatic tissues is maintained in a highly-methylated state, and (2) this 5' Utr region has a consensus sequence that differs from that of clones made using standard host strains and that is suggestive of an open reading frame.

the consensus of the DNA sequence of the ends of the 5' region, which is a CpG-rich region that is highly methylated in somatic tissue, differs from that of the same region in clones made using conventional E. coli host strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning of hyper- and hypomethylated genomic elements and the effect of host strain on the sequence of cloned elements.
the effect of the E. coli host used for cloning on the consensus sequence and methylation state of regions cloned from human DNA.
the role of CpG islands in human L1 transposable elements and their role as a source of genetic variation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consensus sequence of the 5' region from the L1 family is different when the element is hypermethylated in vivo.
the consensus sequence of the 5' region from the L1 transposable element differs significantly between clones made in conventional hosts and clones made in highly methylation tolerant hosts.
, in our hands, cloning of human DNA in E. coli using conventional host strains leads to a loss of CpG dinucleotide methylation and a change in sequence at the ends of the 1,8 kb L1 fragment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sequence of a region of the human genome which is hypermethylated in vivo in somatic tissues, and is therefore likely to be repressed transcriptionally in somatic cells, can be cloned in an unmethylated form using methylation-tolerant hosts.
the consensus sequence of the 5' region is different when clones are made using highly methylation tolerant hosts.
the host strain used in cloning experiments may have a profound influence on the consensus sequence determined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the host strain used to clone DNA can have a profound effect on the sequence of the clones obtained.
the consensus sequence of a CpG island may depend on the host strain used to clone it.
it is essential to use host strains that are tolerant to methylation if the consensus of a region of DNA containing many CpG dinucleotide sequences is to be determined correctly.
